skill.name: write-tech-spec
skill.description: Create a TECH.md specification for a significant Warp feature by researching the current codebase, architecture, and implementation constraints.
skill.summary: Research the repository and turn product intent into a grounded implementation plan.
skill.author: warpdotdev

security_audit.summary: All 27 static detections are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, documentation URLs, or planning language in SKILL.md. The file describes how to write and validate technical specifications; it contains no executable command, network request, or prompt-injection instruction.

remediation.issue: The static analyzer treats inline Markdown code spans and links as external command or network activity.
remediation.suggestion: No security change is required. If reducing scanner noise is important, classify Markdown code spans and documentation-only URLs separately from executable code.

remediation.issue: The skill asks agents to inspect repository structure and coordinate technical planning.
remediation.suggestion: Keep repository inspection scoped to the requested feature, and require explicit user approval before creating tickets or using external services.

content.value_statement: Technical plans often drift from product intent or the current codebase. This skill researches repository structure and turns constraints into an actionable TECH.md implementation plan.
actual_capabilities: Creates a TECH.md specification for a significant Warp feature.
Researches product requirements, repository structure, relevant code, types, and data flow.
Documents proposed module changes, APIs, state, ownership boundaries, and tradeoffs.
Defines testing and validation steps tied to product behavior.
Evaluates parallel work and records coordination boundaries when sub-agents are available.
limitations: It does not implement the feature or modify application source code.
It cannot infer architecture that is absent from the accessible repository.
It does not create tickets or external issues without explicit user approval.
It depends on a product specification for authoritative user-visible behavior.

use_cases.title: Plan a multi-module feature
use_cases.description: Translate an approved product concept into a scoped technical plan with affected modules, data flow, ownership, and tradeoffs.

use_cases.title: Prepare work for implementation
use_cases.description: Give an implementation agent a repository-grounded sequence of changes and concrete validation steps.

use_cases.title: Align reviewers before coding
use_cases.description: Document architecture decisions, risks, testing responsibilities, and optional parallel work before a large change begins.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic specification
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the relevant product specification and repository files. Draft a concise TECH.md with Context, Proposed changes, and Testing and validation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a feature needs its first implementation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Ground the plan in code
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the current code for this feature, identify the main files, types, data flow, and ownership boundaries, then update the TECH.md plan with precise references.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the initial plan may not match the existing architecture.

prompt_templates.title: Add validation coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this technical specification against the product behavior. Add concrete unit, integration, manual, or visual validation steps for every important behavior invariant.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before implementation or review approval.

prompt_templates.title: Design coordinated execution
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate whether parallel sub-agents reduce delivery time for this feature. If useful, define worktrees, branches, ownership boundaries, merge points, and validation ownership in the TECH.md.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for large features with separable workstreams.

output_examples.input: A product specification for vertical tab hover behavior in an existing desktop application.
output_examples.output: A TECH.md plan covering current workspace state, affected modules, proposed event handling, testing steps, and commit-pinned code references.

output_examples.input: A multi-module feature with uncertain implementation ownership.
output: A context section that identifies relevant files and data flow.
A proposed changes section that assigns ownership and explains tradeoffs.
A validation plan linked to the product behavior.

output_examples.input: A large feature with independent frontend and backend work.
output_examples.output: A coordination plan that explains parallel worktrees, branch strategy, synchronization points, and sequential integration checks.

best_practices: Read the product specification and relevant code before proposing architecture.
Use commit-pinned references for important code locations.
Map every important product behavior to a concrete validation step.
anti_patterns: Do not guess about repository architecture when the code can be inspected.
Do not restate product behavior instead of linking the source specification.
Do not propose parallel agents without explicit ownership, worktree, and merge boundaries.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a repository-grounded TECH.md implementation specification for a significant Warp feature.

faq.question: Does it implement the feature?
faq.answer: No. It documents the implementation plan, architecture, tradeoffs, and validation approach.

faq.question: Does it require a PRODUCT.md file?
faq.answer: A PRODUCT.md file is preferred because it anchors user-visible behavior, but the skill can work from available requirements.

faq.question: What repository information does it inspect?
faq.answer: It examines relevant files, types, data flow, ownership boundaries, and the current commit when references are needed.

faq.question: When should I use the parallelization section?
faq.answer: Use it for large features where independent workstreams can reduce delivery time and have clear coordination boundaries.

faq.question: Can it create Linear or GitHub issues?
faq.answer: Only after explicit user approval. Ticket creation is optional and should use the appropriate connected tool.
